audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel chapter 17, first-pass restored draft
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for MT/Greek length differences, Goliath height variants, David's age ambiguity, royal reward, sibling bullying, ethnic rhetoric, animal-killing claims, armor and sling, beheading, corpse exposure, pursuit, plunder, Jerusalem chronology, and Saul's identity questions.

verses.restored: Philistines gathered their camps for battle. They gathered at Socoh of Judah and camped between Socoh and Azekah, at Ephes-dammim.

familiar.text: Now the Philistines gathered together their armies to battle, and were gathered together at Shochoh, which belongeth to Judah, and pitched between Shochoh and Azekah, in Ephesdammim.

verses.restored: Saul and men of Israel gathered and camped in valley of Elah, arranging battle against Philistines.

familiar.text: And Saul and the men of Israel were gathered together, and pitched by the valley of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines.

verses.restored: Philistines stood on mountain on one side, Israel stood on mountain on other side, and valley was between them.

familiar.text: And the Philistines stood on a mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on a mountain on the other side: and there was a valley between them.

verses.restored: A champion came out from camps of Philistines, named Goliath of Gath; his height was six cubits and a span.

familiar.text: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.

verses.restored: A bronze helmet was upon his head, and he wore scale armor; weight of armor was five thousand shekels of bronze.

familiar.text: And he had an helmet of brass upon his head, and he was armed with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of brass.

verses.restored: Bronze greaves were upon his legs, and a bronze javelin was slung between his shoulders.

familiar.text: And he had greaves of brass upon his legs, and a target of brass between his shoulders.

verses.restored: Shaft of his spear was like weaver's beam, iron of spearhead weighed six hundred shekels, and shield-bearer went before him.

familiar.text: And the staff of his spear was like a weaver’s beam; and his spear’s head weighed six hundred shekels of iron: and one bearing a shield went before him.

verses.restored: He stood and called to Israel's ranks, saying, Why have you come out to arrange battle? Am I not Philistine, and are you not servants of Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.

familiar.text: And he stood and cried unto the armies of Israel, and said unto them, Why are ye come out to set your battle in array? am not I a Philistine, and ye servants to Saul? choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me.

verses.restored: If he is able to fight with me and strike me, we will become your servants; but if I prevail and strike him, you will become our servants and serve us.

familiar.text: If he be able to fight with me, and to kill me, then will we be your servants: but if I prevail against him, and kill him, then shall ye be our servants, and serve us.

verses.restored: Philistine said, I defy ranks of Israel this day. Give me a man, and let us fight together.

familiar.text: And the Philistine said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together.

verses.restored: Saul and all Israel heard these words of Philistine, and they were shattered and greatly afraid.

familiar.text: When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.

verses.restored: David was son of an Ephrathite man from Bethlehem in Judah, whose name was Jesse, who had eight sons. In days of Saul, the man was old, advanced among men.

familiar.text: Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehemjudah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons: and the man went among men for an old man in the days of Saul.

verses.restored: Three oldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to battle. Names of his three sons who went were Eliab firstborn, Abinadab second, and Shammah third.

familiar.text: And the three eldest sons of Jesse went and followed Saul to the battle: and the names of his three sons that went to the battle were Eliab the firstborn, and next unto him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.

verses.restored: David was youngest. The three oldest went after Saul.

familiar.text: And David was the youngest: and the three eldest followed Saul.

verses.restored: David went back and forth from Saul to tend flock of his father at Bethlehem.

familiar.text: But David went and returned from Saul to feed his father’s sheep at Bethlehem.

verses.restored: Philistine drew near morning and evening and presented himself forty days.

familiar.text: And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and presented himself forty days.

verses.restored: Jesse said to David his son, Take for your brothers an ephah of this roasted grain and these ten loaves, and run to camp to your brothers.

familiar.text: And Jesse said unto David his son, Take now for thy brethren an ephah of this parched corn, and these ten loaves, and run to the camp to thy brethren.

verses.restored: Bring these ten portions of cheese to commander of thousand. Visit your brothers for well-being, and take their pledge.

familiar.text: And carry these ten cheeses unto the captain of their thousand, and look how thy brethren fare, and take their pledge.

verses.restored: Saul, they, and all men of Israel were in valley of Elah, fighting with Philistines.

familiar.text: Now Saul, and they, and all the men of Israel, were in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.

verses.restored: David rose early in morning, left flock with keeper, carried supplies, and went as Jesse commanded him. He came to wagon-circle as army was going out to battle line and raising war cry.

familiar.text: And David rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and took, and went, as Jesse had commanded him; and he came to the trench, as the host was going forth to the fight, and shouted for the battle.

verses.restored: Israel and Philistines arranged rank against rank.

familiar.text: For Israel and the Philistines had put the battle in array, army against army.

verses.restored: David left baggage from upon him in hand of baggage keeper, ran to battle line, and came and asked his brothers about well-being.

familiar.text: And David left his carriage in the hand of the keeper of the carriage, and ran into the army, and came and saluted his brethren.

verses.restored: As he spoke with them, champion came up—Goliath Philistine from Gath by name—from ranks of Philistines, and spoke according to same words. David heard.

familiar.text: And as he talked with them, behold, there came up the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, out of the armies of the Philistines, and spake according to the same words: and David heard them.

verses.restored: All men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from before him and were greatly afraid.

familiar.text: And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were sore afraid.

verses.restored: Men of Israel said, Have you seen this man who comes up? He comes up to defy Israel. The man who strikes him, king will enrich with great wealth, give him his daughter, and make house of his father free in Israel.

familiar.text: And the men of Israel said, Have ye seen this man that is come up? surely to defy Israel is he come up: and it shall be, that the man who killeth him, the king will enrich him with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and make his father’s house free in Israel.

verses.restored: David said to men standing with him, What will be done for man who strikes this Philistine and turns aside disgrace from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine that he defies ranks of living Divine?

familiar.text: And David spake to the men that stood by him, saying, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?

verses.restored: People answered him according to this word, saying, Thus shall it be done for man who strikes him.

familiar.text: And the people answered him after this manner, saying, So shall it be done to the man that killeth him.

verses.restored: Eliab his oldest brother heard when he spoke to men, and Eliab's anger burned against David. He said, Why did you come down, and with whom did you leave those few sheep in wilderness? I know your presumption and evil of your heart, for you came down to see battle.

familiar.text: And Eliab his eldest brother heard when he spake unto the men; and Eliab’s anger was kindled against David, and he said, Why camest thou down hither? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart; for thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle.

verses.restored: David said, What have I done now? Was it not only a word?

familiar.text: And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause?

verses.restored: He turned from beside him toward another and spoke according to same word, and people returned an answer as first word.

familiar.text: And he turned from him toward another, and spake after the same manner: and the people answered him again after the former manner.

verses.restored: Words David spoke were heard and reported before Saul, and he sent for him.

familiar.text: And when the words were heard which David spake, they rehearsed them before Saul: and he sent for him.

verses.restored: David said to Saul, Let no human heart fall because of him. Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine.

familiar.text: And David said to Saul, Let no man’s heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.

verses.restored: Saul said to David, You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for you are a youth and he is a man of war from his youth.

familiar.text: And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.

verses.restored: David said to Saul, Your servant was tending his father's flock. Lion or bear came and carried a sheep from flock.

familiar.text: And David said unto Saul, Thy servant kept his father’s sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock:

verses.restored: I went out after it, struck it, and rescued from its mouth. When it rose against me, I seized its beard, struck it, and put it to death.

familiar.text: And I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth: and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him.

verses.restored: Your servant struck both lion and bear. This uncircumcised Philistine shall be like one of them, because he defied ranks of living Divine.

familiar.text: Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God.

verses.restored: David said, YHWH who rescued me from hand of lion and hand of bear will rescue me from hand of this Philistine. Saul said to David, Go, and may YHWH be with you.

familiar.text: David said moreover, The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and the LORD be with thee.

verses.restored: Saul clothed David with his garments, placed a bronze helmet upon his head, and clothed him with armor.

familiar.text: And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail.

verses.restored: David girded his sword over his garments and tried to walk, because he had not tested them. David said to Saul, I cannot walk in these, because I have not tested them. David removed them from upon him.

familiar.text: And David girded his sword upon his armour, and he assayed to go; for he had not proved it. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him.

verses.restored: He took his staff in his hand, chose five smooth stones from wadi, put them in shepherd's bag he had—in pouch—and his sling was in his hand. He drew near to Philistine.

familiar.text: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd’s bag which he had, even in a scrip; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.

verses.restored: Philistine came, coming and drawing near to David, and man bearing shield was before him.

familiar.text: And the Philistine came on and drew near unto David; and the man that bare the shield went before him.

verses.restored: Philistine looked and saw David and despised him, because he was a youth, ruddy, and beautiful in appearance.

familiar.text: And when the Philistine looked about, and saw David, he disdained him: for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and of a fair countenance.

verses.restored: Philistine said to David, Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks? Philistine cursed David by his gods.

familiar.text: And the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.

verses.restored: Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give your flesh to birds of heavens and animals of field.

familiar.text: And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field.

verses.restored: David said to Philistine, You come to me with sword, spear, and javelin, but I come to you in name of YHWH of armies, Divine of ranks of Israel, whom you have defied.

familiar.text: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.

verses.restored: This day YHWH will deliver you into my hand. I will strike you, remove your head from upon you, and give corpses of Philistine camp this day to birds of heavens and animals of earth, so all earth may know there is Divine for Israel.

familiar.text: This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee, and take thine head from thee; and I will give the carcases of the host of the Philistines this day unto the fowls of the air, and to the wild beasts of the earth; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.

verses.restored: All this assembly shall know that YHWH does not save by sword or spear, because battle belongs to YHWH, and he will give you into our hand.

familiar.text: And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD’s, and he will give you into our hands.

verses.restored: When Philistine arose and came and drew near to meet David, David hurried and ran toward battle line to meet Philistine.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when the Philistine arose, and came, and drew nigh to meet David, that David hastened, and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.

verses.restored: David put his hand into bag, took from there a stone, slung it, and struck Philistine on forehead. Stone sank into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to ground.

familiar.text: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.

verses.restored: David prevailed over Philistine with sling and stone, struck Philistine, and put him to death. There was no sword in David's hand.

familiar.text: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.

verses.restored: David ran, stood over Philistine, took his sword, drew it from sheath, put him to death, and cut off his head with it. Philistines saw their champion was dead and fled.

familiar.text: Therefore David ran, and stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of the sheath thereof, and slew him, and cut off his head therewith. And when the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled.

verses.restored: Men of Israel and Judah arose, shouted, and pursued Philistines as far as entrance of valley and gates of Ekron. Wounded Philistines fell along road of Shaaraim as far as Gath and Ekron.

familiar.text: And the men of Israel and of Judah arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines, until thou come to the valley, and to the gates of Ekron. And the wounded of the Philistines fell down by the way to Shaaraim, even unto Gath, and unto Ekron.

verses.restored: Children of Israel returned from hot pursuit of Philistines and plundered their camp.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel returned from chasing after the Philistines, and they spoiled their tents.

verses.restored: David took head of Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, but he put his weapons in his tent.

familiar.text: And David took the head of the Philistine, and brought it to Jerusalem; but he put his armour in his tent.

verses.restored: When Saul saw David going out to meet Philistine, he said to Abner commander of army, Whose son is this youth, Abner? Abner said, As your life, king, I do not know.

familiar.text: And when Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine, he said unto Abner, the captain of the host, Abner, whose son is this youth? And Abner said, As thy soul liveth, O king, I cannot tell.

verses.restored: King said, Ask whose son this young man is.

familiar.text: And the king said, Enquire thou whose son the stripling is.

verses.restored: When David returned from striking Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with head of Philistine in his hand.

familiar.text: And as David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, Abner took him, and brought him before Saul with the head of the Philistine in his hand.

verses.restored: Saul said to him, Whose son are you, youth? David said, Son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.

familiar.text: And Saul said to him, Whose son art thou, thou young man? And David answered, I am the son of thy servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.

translation_notes: The chapter exists in substantially shorter form in important Greek witnesses; verses and narrative seams involving David's prior court service, the reward, and Saul's questions require source-witness audit.
Goliath's reported height differs across witnesses. Physical size is narrative military description, not proof of moral worth, monstrosity, disability, or Divine rejection.
David is called a youth, but his precise age is not given. This story must not romanticize child soldiers, recruit minors into danger, or teach that courage means accepting adult warfare.
Eliab's contempt and Goliath's ridicule are bullying and status enforcement. Sibling conflict, age, skin tone, beauty, height, and body size must not be used to shame people.
'Uncircumcised Philistine' is ancient covenant-war rhetoric and may not become an ethnic, religious, or bodily slur against living people.
The challenge, reward, royal daughter, and household exemption show political and economic incentives surrounding David's choice; the scene is not a pure individual duel outside systems of power.
David rejects unfamiliar armor but still uses a lethal ranged weapon. The narrative does not teach weapon invulnerability, magical stones, or that faith makes safety planning unnecessary.
The beheading, corpse exposure, pursuit, casualties, and plunder are battlefield violence. They may not be glorified, imitated, or sanitized into harmless children's entertainment.
Verse 47 critiques trust in military technology, yet the narrative still culminates in killing. It cannot authorize holy war, vigilantism, ethnic violence, or leader cults.
Saul's questions about David's father likely concern household identity and reward obligations; they also participate in source tensions with chapter 16.
safety_note: Do not use David and Goliath to bully bodies, shame fear, recruit children, glorify weapons, promise supernatural invulnerability, or label a modern group as Philistines. David's courage does not erase the political rewards, battlefield deaths, beheading, corpse exposure, pursuit, or plunder. The story cannot justify holy war, vigilantism, racial or religious contempt, or the claim that a favored young hero is beyond accountability.
